newsitem.title: UK: How stock markets overseas did.
newsitem.headline: How stock markets overseas did.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Leading British stocks ended with moderate losses as the Dow got off to a wobbly start after a 148-point plunge Friday. The benchmark FTSE 100 index of leading shares shed 19.0 points to settle at 4,251.7, as decliners beat advancers by a margin of two to one.

FRANKFURT - Stocks took a sharp dive after Wall Street's tumble Friday unnerved the market and reignited concerns on U.S. inflation and the risk of higher U.S. interest rates. The 30-share blue chip DAX index closed the floor session down 60.15 points at 3,279.90 points, although the market pared its losses in the post-bourse session on the firm dollar. The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade, ended the day down 21.72 points at 3,297.52 points.
PARIS - Stocks finished slightly lower after mirroring a second day of selling on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.43 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,566.13.

ZURICH - Stocks recovered from a weak opening to close only slightly easier. Major investors stayed away from the market, but Swiss stocks drew some support from the firmer dollar. Dealers said that, although the market shrugged off Wall Street's losses, the U.S. stock market was likely to determine future developments. The Broad SPI lost 10.97 to end at 2,906.88.

TOKYO - Stocks, especially in the construction sector, were hurt by sales aimed at dissolving cross-shareholdings. A sharp decline in Wall Street stocks Friday invited selling of blue chips in Tokyo to collect profits, also accelerating the overall downturn. The 225-share Nikkei average shed 154.51 points to close at 17,692.47.

HONG KONG - Stocks fell to a sharply lower close, prompted by a drop on Wall Street and weakness in the local property market. The Hang Seng Index closed 220.63 points, or 1.76 percent, lower at 12,295.97, after clawing back some ground from a low of 12,264.76.

SYDNEY - Stocsk ended mildly weaker in a muted reaction to a sharp sell-off Friday on Wall Street, which followed a surprising jump in U.S. wholesale prices. The Australian Stock Exchange's benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 14.4 points lower at 2,366.1, well off its intraday low of 2,349.1.

JOHANNESBURG - Anxiety over Wall Street and weak local bonds weighed down stocks, which finished weaker. Dealers added that local stocks were holding up well in the wake of the Dow's plunge Friday. The all-share index fell 55.6 points to 6,966.4 and the industrial index shed 47.2 points to 8,166.8 points. The gold index was off 23.8 points at 1,283.
